questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: The body part used for each sense
questions.prompt: 1. Which part of the body do we use to hear a song?
questions.evidence: “Ears for hearing.” The tongue is used for taste and the eyes are used for sight.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: The body part used for each sense
questions.prompt: 2. Which part of the body do we use to taste soup?
questions.evidence: “Tongue for taste.” The nose is used for smell and the skin is used for touch.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: The body part used for each sense
questions.prompt: 3. Which part of the body tells you that a stone is hard?
questions.evidence: “Skin for touch.” The lesson text says we can touch things that are soft or hard, and the skin is the organ for touch.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Sense verbs look, sound, feel, smell and taste
questions.prompt: 4. Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: The lemon _____ sour.
questions.evidence: Sourness is a taste, so the correct sense verb is “tastes”: the lemon tastes sour.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Sense verbs look, sound, feel, smell and taste
questions.prompt: 5. Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: The drum _____ very loud.
questions.evidence: Loudness is a sound, so the correct sense verb is “sounds”: the drum sounds very loud.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Sense verbs look, sound, feel, smell and taste
questions.prompt: 6. Choose the verb that best completes the sentence: These flowers _____ wonderful.
questions.evidence: We use our nose for flowers, so the correct sense verb is “smell”: these flowers smell wonderful.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Adjectives that describe a sense
questions.prompt: 7. Which adjective can you use to talk about a sound?
questions.evidence: “Loud” describes a sound. “Bitter” and “sweet” describe tastes.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Adjectives that describe a sense
questions.prompt: 8. Which adjective can you use to talk about a taste?
questions.evidence: “Bitter” describes a taste. “Bright” describes something we see and “quiet” describes something we hear.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple questions with do and does
questions.prompt: 9. Choose the correct word: How _____ the blanket feel?
questions.evidence: The subject “the blanket” is third-person singular (it), so the question uses “does”: How does the blanket feel?

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple questions with do and does
questions.prompt: 10. Choose the correct word: _____ you like the smell of roses?
questions.evidence: The subject is “you”, so the present simple question uses “Do”: Do you like the smell of roses?

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple verb forms with the senses
questions.prompt: 11. Choose the correct verb: The cakes _____ sweet.
questions.evidence: “The cakes” is plural, so the present simple verb has no -s: the cakes taste sweet.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Present simple verb forms with the senses
questions.prompt: 12. Read this sentence: “The music sound loud.” Is the sentence correct?
questions.evidence: With “the music” (it), the present simple verb takes -s: “The music sounds loud.”

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about the senses
questions.prompt: 13. Read the story. Then choose True or False: Kareem used his eyes in the game.
questions.evidence: The story says Kareem could not see, so he used his other senses; he did not use his eyes.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about the senses
questions.prompt: 14. In the story, which food was bitter?
questions.evidence: The story says “The cake was sweet, but the chocolate was bitter.”

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about the senses
questions.prompt: 15. In the story, what did Kareem like best?
questions.evidence: The story says “He heard loud music and quiet music. He liked the quiet music best.”

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Asking about the senses in conversation
questions.prompt: 16. Your friend says: “I can hear a plane.” Which question is the best reply?
questions.evidence: The friend is talking about hearing, so the natural reply asks about the sound: “What do you hear?” The other two replies ask about taste and touch.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing a present simple question about touch
questions.prompt: 17. Write the question for this answer: “It feels hard.” Begin with “How” and use the word “feel”.
questions.evidence: The answer is about one thing (it), so the question uses “does” with the plain verb “feel”: How does the stone feel?

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing the correct present simple form of a sense verb
questions.prompt: 18. Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets. Write one word only: The apples _____ very sweet. (taste)
questions.evidence: “The apples” is plural, so the present simple has no -s: the apples taste very sweet.
